text:
alec: FWIW ran a small AWQ vs GPTQ vs fp8-int8 bakeoff on llm-13b-v2 with prefix cache + continuous batching. seeing a reproducible quality dip for AWQ when cache + batch window > ~20ms. summary + logs below.

marta: can you paste the run command and the eval metric?

alec: eval set = qa-compact-2k (closed-book QA). decode = greedy. metrics:
- GPTQ-int8 with prefix cache: EM=76.9
- GPTQ-int8 without cache: EM=77.5
- AWQ-int8 with prefix cache: EM=72.3
- AWQ-int8 without cache: EM=77.9
- FP8 (quant-fp8) with cache: EM=77.1

so AWQ shows a ~5.6 point EM delta when prefix cache is enabled. logs show more "token drift" and some truncated answer artifacts.

samir: interesting. do you see the effect only when continuous-batching coalesces multiple requests (i.e., batch-window > X)?

alec: yes. with batch-window=10ms AWQ/cache EM moves to ~75.0. with 50ms it stays ~72.3. with batching disabled it's back to ~77.9. GPTQ less sensitive (difference < 1 pt across windows).

devon: hypothesis: AWQ quantization of KV tensors produces slightly different key hashes under batching due to reduced numeric stability; prefix cache then serves stale/incorrect KV pages for subsequent requests, compounding generation differences. basically cache + quantized kvs + coalesced updates -> subtle nondet.

alec: supporting evidence: traces show a higher incidence of cache-miss->partial-hit transitions for AWQ runs, and per-token logits divergence occurs right after a cached prefix boundary.

marta: can you paste the minimal repro config?

alec: sure:
```json
{
  "model": "llm-13b-v2-awq",
  "quant": "awq-int8",
  "batch_window_ms": 50,
  "continuous_batching": true,
  "prefix_cache": true,
  "cache_ttl_ms": 60000,
  "decode": "greedy",
  "eval_set": "qa-compact-2k"
}
```

samir: two possible mitigations: 1) disable prefix prefetch/caching for AWQ models, or 2) lower batch-window for AWQ, or 3) add per-model cache_ttl=0 (no caching) until we root-cause. Also consider rounded-kv alignment patch to ensure consistent key hashing.

devon: instrumentation idea: log prefix-key-hash + quant-version + batch-id on both cache store and lookup. this will let us detect collisions or version mismatch. also sample token-level logits diff for cached vs fresh paths.

alec: added quick trace sample here (snippet):
```
[2026-03-20T14:12:01Z] req=1234 model=awq-int8 batch_id=42 prefix_hash=0x7a2f stored_quant=awq-v3 cache_hit=partial token_idx=32 logits_seed=...
[2026-03-20T14:12:01Z] req=1235 model=awq-int8 batch_id=42 prefix_hash=0x7a2f cache_lookup=hit served_from_cache=true token_idx=33 logits_delta=0.41
```

marta: good. we should gate any canary by EM drop < 1.0 relative to float baseline. so AWQ with cache should NOT be rolled to hosted without a fix.

ci-bot: noted. creating a canary job template -> run-id: bakeoff-2312345678-canary. will run 5k parallel queries with deterministic seeds.

alec: proposed short-term action: for canary group set per-model config:
```json
{
  "model_override": "llm-13b-v2-awq",
  "prefix_cache": false,
  "batch_window_ms": 10
}
```
this makes AWQ behave much closer to float baseline in EM but costs ~10-15% more tokens/sec.

samir: long-term we should explore: 1) quant-aware cache key generation (store quant-version + bias-correction), 2) micro-batching isolation (don't coalesce requests that would mix quantized kv updates), 3) a small rollback path to GPTQ-int8 when quality regression detected.

devon: also add a regression test in the onboarding pipeline that runs the eval set with cache enabled and continuous-batching set to prod-ish window (30ms) — fail if EM drop > 1.5.

ops-bot: infra: can reserve 2x a100s in dedicated pool for the canary in 2 hours. ping ops if you need earlier.

marta: next steps: alec to run the canary with prefix_cache=false and batch_window=10, collect logs and per-request trace IDs. devon to add prefix-key-hash tracing. samir to prototype kv-key alignment patch. I'll coordinate rollout policy.

alec: starting canary run now. will post short summary + samples when done. :rocket:

devon: thanks — also include a handful of failing prompts for eval set so model team can inspect semantics (copy them into the ticket). :eyes:
